misconception_description: Student believes that variable identifiers can only be one letter long.

solutions.generated_code:
program DamagePokemon
kamus
  p, q : string
  l, m : integer
  e : real
  s, g : integer
algoritma
  input(p, l)
  input(q, m)
  if p == q then
    e <- 1
  else if p == "fire" and q == "grass" then
    e <- 2
  else if p == "grass" and q == "water" then
    e <- 2
  else if p == "water" and q == "fire" then
    e <- 2
  else
    e <- 0.5
  endif
  s <- l - m
  g <- bulat(((2 * l) / 5 + 2) * (l / m) * e * s / 10)
  if g < 1 then
    g <- 1
  endif
  output(g)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: All variable identifiers have been reduced to single letters to reflect the student's belief that variable names can only be one letter long. The mappings are: attacker->a, defender->d, attacker_type->t, attacker_level->l, defender_type->u, defender_level->m, level_diff->n, effectiveness->e. The code functions identically to the original but with significantly reduced readability. The student believes this is the correct and only way to name variables in programming.
